detail.title: From Stocks to Bricks: The Housing Market Effects of Dividend Tax Hikes
detail.abstract: This paper examines how dividend taxation affects real estate markets by influencing household portfolio allocation, prompting a shift from equity investments toward real estate assets. We exploit both long-run national variation in U.S. dividend tax schedules and predetermined cross-county and cross-income-group exposure to the 2013 U.S. dividend tax hike. Using both county and county–income-group level panels covering 2005–2020, higher marginal dividend tax rates are associated with greater mortgage demand and higher house-price growth. An event-study difference-in-differences design around the 2013 reform confirms these patterns causally: affected high-income households show a significant increase in mortgage demand, and a one percentage point tax increase raises annual house-price returns by 0.126pp, with larger effects in supply-constrained markets. Rents also rise, indicating spillovers into broader housing affordability. These results highlight an important unintended consequence of capital-income taxation: policies aimed at taxing equity returns can propagate into local housing markets, amplifying demand and exacerbating affordability pressures, especially in areas with limited housing supply.

title: The Environment as ‘Human Family Heritage’. Taking Seriously Legal Technical Terms
affiliations: Catholic University of America (CUA)

detail.title: The Environment as ‘Human Family Heritage’. Taking Seriously Legal Technical Terms
detail.abstract: This article argues that the natural environment should be understood in legal terms as the family heritage of humanity. Recognizing the environment in this way helps to resolve several doctrinal challenges in intergenerational justice and carries significant implications for both national and international law. Drawing on the biblical account of the cosmos given to Adam and Eve, and exploring parallels in Catholic social teaching, Roman law, Indigenous cosmologies, and modern international treaties, this study identifies a persistent yet under-developed legal logic that treats nature as an intergenerational patrimony. After delineating the concept of family heritage and outlining its key characteristics (such as collective ownership, purpose orientation, protection of essential goods, and public-order status), this article presents ten normative consequences. These include: applying a parental standard of environmental stewardship, prioritizing the protection of vulnerable family members, establishing a duty to preserve and enhance common wealth (the heritage), reframing the concept of private property, and expanding the international law principle of “common heritage of humanity”. This article concludes that, from a legal standpoint, how the environment should be treated as part of humanity’s family heritage.

title: Not Fannie and Freddie: Wall Street's Trillion-Dollar Fraud Machine Inside the Machines of Mortgage Madness, Derivatives, and the CDS Time Bomb

detail.abstract: This paper challenges the conventional narrative that government-sponsored enterprises (GSEs) and affordable housing policies caused the 2008 financial crisis. Through detailed analysis of the origination, securitization, and distribution chain, I demonstrate that private-label mortgage-backed securities and the unregulated credit default swap market were the primary drivers of the crisis. The evidence shows that toxic loan products-including no-documentation loans and hybrid adjustable-rate mortgages with payment shocks exceeding 70%-were deliberately engineered by private originators operating under perverse fee-based incentive structures. Investment banks securitized these loans while conducting inadequate due diligence, creating complex collateralized debt obligations that amplified systemic risk. The $62 trillion credit default swap market, particularly AIG's $500 billion in mortgagerelated exposure, transformed a housing bubble into a global financial catastrophe through counterparty contagion. GSE participation in risky lending came late (2005-2007) and remained modest compared to private-sector dominance. Analysis of the 2023 Silicon Valley Bank and Credit Suisse failures reveals that fundamental vulnerabilities-liquidity mismatches, concentration risk, regulatory forbearance, and moral hazard-persist fifteen years later, suggesting regulatory reforms have addressed symptoms while leaving causal mechanisms largely intact.

detail.abstract: We propose a generalized multivariate unobserved components model to decompose macroeconomic data into trend and cyclical components. We then forecast the series using Bayesian methods. We document that a fully Bayesian estimation, that accounts for state and parameter uncertainty, allows for stochastic volatility components in variables, exploits cross-sectional information, and use the commonalities across variables, consistently dominates out-of-sample forecasts produced by alternative multivariate and univariate models. The proposed method yields results with research or policy relevant applications and sensible interpretations. Finally, we find that while outperforming individual univariate specifications, an optimally pooled univariate model does not outperform the benchmark model.

title: Who Enters the Pipeline to Partnership at Leading American Law Firms?

detail.title: Who Enters the Pipeline to Partnership at Leading American Law Firms?
detail.abstract: One in six lawyers obtain highly selective positions after law school that serve as the primary pipeline to an important leadership position with great influence and wealth: a partner in America's leading law firms. We investigate who enters this pipeline using novel data on the first job of law school graduates from 1992 to 2023. We first study educational backgrounds and find that a long-run trend of increasing market concentration among the most selective law schools reversed in the late-2010s, driven by hiring practices expanding to include more lawyers from underrepresented minority groups from a wider range of law schools. We then study how and why diversity has changed and find that gender diversity increased by almost a third and racial diversity more than tripled. Diversity historically increased from greater access to legal education, but it has also more recently increased from improvements in placement rates relative to law school peers. Overall, the results underscore the central role of law schools, law firms, and judges in shaping who ultimately holds some of the most important and influential positions in the legal profession, as institutional admissions decisions and hiring practices directly affect who enters the primary pipeline.

title: The Sharpe–Parity Principle: A Sharpe-Based Framework for Real-World Option Pricing

detail.title: The Sharpe–Parity Principle: A Sharpe-Based Framework for Real-World Option Pricing
detail.abstract:
This paper develops the Sharpe–Parity Principle (SPP) as an equilibrium framework for derivative pricing in real-world markets. The SPP postulates that risk-adjusted excess returns remain approximately equal across linearly dependent portfolios, representing an empirical regularity of financial equilibrium rather than a universal law. From this condition, the Sharpe–Consistency Pricing (SCP) identity emerges as a real-world valuation formula that requires no risk-neutral transformation or PDE.

Under ideal replication (E[RI] = Rf, σD = σI), SCP reduces to the Black–Scholes–Merton (BSM) price, making BSM the limiting equilibrium of perfect Sharpe consistency. Two key advantages of SCP are: (i) compatibility with arbitrary return distributions (including fat-tailed and skewed empirical distributions), and (ii) explicit incorporation of the equity risk premium through the Sharpe adjustment term. In the empirical study of covered-call ETFs (Shin 2025a), the Upside Lottery Discount(ULD) is observed as a systematic deviation from Sharpe parity, providing real-world evidence consistent with the SPP framework. This paper presents the theoretical foundation; numerical calibration and empirical validation will follow as future work.

title: Legally Supported Bullying? Legal Consciousness on Non-compete Agreements in China

declarations.ethicsApproval: This research has been examined and approved by the Research Committee from City University of Hong Kong (Approval Number: HU-STA-00001028).

detail.abstract: There are growing scandals involving Chinese companies abusing non-compete agreements (non-competes). Using legal consciousness as the research framework, this article empirically explores employees' perceptions, interactions, and experiences with non-competes. Drawing on twenty semi-structured interviews and 344 supplementary screenshots of online discussions, this study identifies complex and intertwined forms of legal consciousness across three moments: signing, considering job hopping, and confronting activated non-competes. Employees may exhibit a "before the law" consciousness by endorsing the theoretical reasonableness of non-competes but simultaneously express a strong "under the law" consciousness in response to their overreach. Legally literate employees mobilize a "with the law" consciousness to seek remedies, while senior employees leverage resources in an "against the law" consciousness to evade enforcement. More commonly, employees develop voluntary or involuntary legal alienation, refraining from resorting to law, which enriches the framework of legal consciousness. The distorted "law in action" highlights the urgent needs for legal reforms.

title: Can Individualized Student Supports Improve Economic Outcomes for Children in High Poverty Schools?
affiliations: Cornell University,  and Government of the United States of America - Bureau of the Census

detail.title: Can Individualized Student Supports Improve Economic Outcomes for Children in High Poverty Schools?
detail.abstract: How can we improve outcomes for low-income students? We analyze the adult earnings impacts of the largest comprehensive student support program in the United States. Communities in Schools (CIS) places a "navigator" in high-poverty schools who provides an integrated system of supports to students, including academic (e.g., tutoring), economic (e.g., access to food assistance, housing), and mentoring. In 2023, CIS worked with 1.8 million students in 3,750 schools. Using later-treated CIS schools as a control, we estimate that four years of exposure to CIS generates a $1,500 (6% of control mean) increase in earnings at age 30. Effects are larger for students from low-income families and are driven by a reduction in non-employment and an increase in the probability of having a low-paying job. Each child exposed to four years of CIS is expected to pay an additional $9,000 in taxes between ages 18-65, which compares favorably to the direct cost of the program. Our results are relevant for the growing community school movement and illuminate a possible path for improving economic mobility in low opportunity neighborhoods.

detail.title: Division of Labor in the Global Economy

publicationDetails.journalName: NBER Working Paper Series

detail.abstract:
This paper links globalization, worker efficiency, and wage inequality within plants to internal labor market organization. Using German plant-worker data and information on the task content of occupations, we document that larger plants (i) use more occupations, (ii) assign fewer tasks per occupation, and (iii) exhibit greater wage dispersion. We develop a model where plants endogenously bundle tasks into occupations, improving worker-task matching at the cost of higher fixed span-of-control costs. Embedding this into a Melitz framework, we show that trade increases worker efficiency and wage inequality in exporting plants, whereas non-exporting plants experience the opposite effects. Structural estimation and simulations confirm the model’s predictions and point to non-monotonic economy-wide effects.

title: The Consequences of Abortion Funding Bans

detail.title: The Consequences of Abortion Funding Bans

detail.abstract:
Do restrictions on public funding create unintended reliance on social assistance? In this paper, we study the 1976 Hyde Amendment, which barred federal funding for abortion. Using county-level data and an event-study design, we show that reduced federal funding for abortion increased fertility among young women by 2%. These effects were concentrated among non-white women, who subsequently experienced greater welfare participation in states with larger abortion funding declines. The consequences extend into the next generation: non-white girls born after Hyde were more likely to rely on public assistance in adulthood. Abortion funding restrictions reinforce long-run economic inequality across generations.

We conduct a large-scale information randomized controlled trial to study fiscal policy impacts. Surveying approximately 9,000 households across five eurozone countries with varying debt-to-GDP ratios enables a clean cross-country comparison. The key finding is that the fiscal multiplier depends jointly on the financing method and the country’s debt burden: multipliers are smaller in high-debt countries when debt-financed but remain similar across countries when tax-financed. Finally, we develop a New Keynesian model featuring fiscal discipline, which reproduces the empirical patterns observed in the survey and highlights their underlying economic mechanisms.

title: Range-Clearing and the Illusion of Sticky Prices : A Microfoundation Based on Subjective Value

detail.title: Range-Clearing and the Illusion of Sticky Prices : A Microfoundation Based on Subjective Value
detail.abstract: This paper challenges the conventional macroeconomic notion of "sticky prices" by introducing a more nuanced, micro-foundational theory of market clearing rooted in Austrian subjective value theory. We begin by deconstructing the traditional concept of equilibrium as a precise, mathematical "point," arguing instead that human valuation is an inherently subjective "range" of acceptability. Consequently, we propose a new definition of market clearing—"range-clearing"—where a market is considered cleared as long as the transacted price falls within the overlapping acceptance ranges of all participants. Armed with this framework, we re-examine the sterile definitional dispute between Monetary Disequilibrium Theory (MDT) and its purist Austrian critics, arguing that a more productive inquiry focuses on "friction" as a neutral starting point. We then demonstrate that the frictions commonly cited as evidence of market failure—such as menu costs, long-term contracts, and reputational concerns—are not external impediments, but are in fact manifestations of rational actors performing cost-benefit calculations within their clearing range. A seller's "hesitation" to change a price is not a sign of market failure, but a testament to the fact that the market is still functioning optimally under real-world transactional costs. By providing a robust, micro-foundational explanation for the phenomenon of price rigidity without resorting to a theory of market failure, this paper fundamentally dismantles the primary justification for activist monetary and fiscal policies. We conclude with a call for a paradigm shift in macroeconomics, urging the discipline to move away from its "mechanical failure" metaphor and to return to a more realistic, human-action-based understanding of market coordination.

detail.abstract: As the risk of climate overshoot grows, attention increasingly turns to climate interventions, such as Solar Radiation Modification (SRM) and Carbon Dioxide Removal (CDR), that is, technologies designed to actively alter the climate system beyond conventional mitigation and adaptation. The article addresses questions of institutional legitimacy and recognition justice, the implications of international legal fragmentation, competing approaches to risk analysis, the application of precautionary and prevention principles, market governance of CDR, the role of intellectual property regimes, and regional perspectives. The most striking tension centres on how risks should be analysed and compared. Climate intervention governance does not exist in a vacuum. Still, it is an emerging field shaped by partial institutional coverage, normative contestation, and private-sector acceleration against a background of limited public salience. This article situates climate intervention governance within broader debates on risk regulation. Building on and critically synthesizing the contributions published in the European Journal of Risk Regulation’s Special Issue devoted to the governance challenges posed by SRM and CDR, the article identifies cross-cutting themes that will shape governance debates in the coming years. It concludes that climate intervention governance is ultimately a test case for contemporary risk analysis and regulation, as well as collective self-governance, under conditions of radical uncertainty.

title: Graph Neural Network Assisted Genetic Algorithm for Structural Dynamic Response and Parameter Optimization

detail.title: Graph Neural Network Assisted Genetic Algorithm for Structural Dynamic Response and Parameter Optimization
detail.abstract: The optimization of structural parameters, such as mass (m), stiffness (k), and damping coefficient (c), is critical for designing efficient, resilient, and stable structures. Conventional numerical approaches, including Finite Element Method (FEM) and Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) simulations, provide high-fidelity results but are computationally expensive for iterative optimization tasks, as each evaluation requires solving the governing equations for every parameter combination. This study proposes a hybrid data-driven framework that integrates a Graph Neural Network (GNN) surrogate model with a Genetic Algorithm (GA) optimizer to overcome these challenges. The GNN is trained to accurately learn the nonlinear mapping between structural parameters and dynamic displacement responses, enabling rapid predictions without repeatedly solving the system equations. A dataset of singledegree-of-freedom (SDOF) system responses is generated using the Newmark-Beta method across diverse mass, stiffness, and damping configurations. The GA then searches for globally optimal parameter sets by minimizing predicted displacements and enhancing dynamic stability. Results demonstrate that the GNN-GA framework achieves strong convergence, robust generalization, and significantly reduced computational cost compared to conventional simulations. This approach highlights the effectiveness of combining machine learning surrogates with evolutionary optimization for automated and intelligent structural design.

detail.abstract:
This paper presents the second chapter of the forthcoming book Human Rights and Intellectual Property before the European Courts: A Case Commentary on the Court of Justice of the European Union and the European Court of Human Rights, the first comprehensive guide to how Europe’s highest courts address the intersection of intellectual property (IP) and human rights. This chapter analyses the relationship between freedom of expression and intellectual property in European law, focusing on how IP rights are balanced against the privileged yet limited right to free expression under Article 10 of the European Convention on Human Rights and Article 11 of the EU Charter. It outlines the three-part test of the European Court of Human Rights (ECtHR) for assessing interferences with freedom of expression and situates IP protection within the “rights of others” that may justify restrictions.

The chapter then examines copyright and trademark law as the two principal areas in which this conflict has arisen before the ECtHR and the Court of Justice of the European Union (CJEU). In copyright, it highlights the growing engagement of both courts with freedom of expression claims and the divergence between the ECtHR’s acceptance of freedom of expression as an external limitation on copyright and the CJEU’s preference for internal balancing through copyright exceptions interpreted in the light of fundamental rights. In trademark law, it explores disputes over third-party expressive uses and refusals of trademark registration, noting the courts’ increasingly nuanced and contextual approach. Overall, the chapter shows how freedom of expression has become a central, though differently framed, constraint on IP protection in Europe.

detail.abstract: Studying microscopic marine organisms is crucial for understanding marine ecosystems, biodiversity, and climate balance. Traditional manual methods for organism identification and counting are time-intensive and prone to error. Existing automated tools, though efficient, are often bulky, costly, and unsuitable for field deployment. This project proposes a portable embedded AI-enabled microscope capable of real-time microorganism detection and counting. The system integrates a digital microscope, a microfluidic sample chip, and an embedded processor (Raspberry Pi/Jetson Nano) running trained CNN models. The model processes live images and accurately identifies organisms on-device without cloud dependency, achieving 96.2% detection accuracy. The proposed setup is compact, energy-efficient, and ideal for marine biology research in real-world field conditions.

title: Latency and the Look-Ahead Bias in Trade and Quote Data
affiliations: University of Notre Dame - Department of Finance, Indiana University - Kelley School of Business - Department of Finance, Wharton Research Data Services (WRDS), University of Notre Dame - Mendoza College of Business and Wharton Research Data Services (WRDS)

detail.title: Latency and the Look-Ahead Bias in Trade and Quote Data
detail.abstract: The NYSE Trade and Quote (TAQ) dataset, used throughout finance research and securities regulation, is generated by a Securities Information Processor (SIP), which aggregates quotes and trades from all U.S. stock exchanges at a central location. We show that the SIP systematically reports events out of sequential order: quote changes that occur after a trade are frequently reported as occurring before the trade. The source of the issue is that trades and quotes are recorded with variable latency (due to, e.g., geography) and are extremely clustered in time. The result is a look-ahead bias: the prevailing SIP quotes, ubiquitous in signing trades and measuring spreads, incorporate price impact from the trade itself. We document that the look-ahead bias leads to incorrect trade signing and downward-biased effective spreads and price impact. The errors are extreme for the large fraction of trades with high reporting latency: approximately 20% of trades are incorrectly signed, and effective spreads and price impact are understated by more than 40%. We propose a signing methodology based on exchange rules that yields 100% accuracy for a significant majority of volume and, over all trades, outperforms existing methodologies.

title: Timing of Algorithmic Advice: Effects on Team Performance and Team Reasoning

detail.abstract: In this paper, we study the impact of algorithmic advice on team decisions through two lab experiments. In Study 1, we vary whether and when advice is provided to a team of that is engaged with a prediction task. We find that decision quality (e.g., team performance) is higher when advice is provided earlier, since it is more readily adopted by the team. We also investigate how algorithmic advice impacts team interactions; we find that early advice leads to a reduction in the teams' efforts to jointly make sense of the problem context and develop mental models linking predictors and outcomes. This points to a downside of early algorithmic advice. In Study 2, in addition to replicating these results, we investigate the impact of algorithmic quality and its interactions with timing. We show that when algorithmic quality is low, the greater reliance on early advice, combined with the reduction in effort for sense-making, diminishes team performance. These findings emphasize the importance of when and how algorithms are introduced into team processes, revealing a fundamental trade-off in human-AI collaboration: early algorithmic advice can improve immediate performance but undermine collective reasoning, whereas delaying advice promotes analytical depth and shared understanding that support long-term team expertise development.

detail.title: The Paradox of Progress: A Study of Pollution, Prosperity, and Property in Indian Cities
detail.abstract: India's urbanization strategy presents two challenges in the country's flagship cities: sustained economic growth and deteriorating air quality. Remarkably, cities with some of the highest levels of air pollution such as Delhi and Mumbai also command the highest residential real estate rates in the country. This paper attempts to study the paradox of real estate values in India's advanced cities wherein greater air pollution coincides with greater pollution levels. This study also looks at the impacts of construction, migration, and infrastructural development in highly polluted cities. It aims to analyse whether these factors would result in property price inflation. The study's results confirmed that urban amenities, economic opportunities, the concentration of infrastructure, and the decline in the environmental quality of cities outweigh in environmental concerns.

title: Administrative Procedural and Litigation Aspects of the Review of Governmental Actions

detail.title: Administrative Procedural and Litigation Aspects of the Review of Governmental Actions
detail.abstract: The main aim of this paper is to investigate the administrative procedural and litigation aspects of judicial review of governmental actions under the scope of the political question doctrine in Hungary. Governmental actions, due to their political nature, are usually excluded from judicial review, which means that an important safeguard of rule of law does not apply to them. As a result, serious constitutional concerns arise, especially when these decisions, in addition to their political nature, have a legal nature, too, or are administrative adjudicative ones. In these cases, procedural safeguards are even more important. The paper therefore examines such borderline cases in the practice of the Hungarian administrative courts and of the Constitutional Court regarding the existence of judicial review in these cases. The research has not comprehensively covered judicial practice, but focuses only on some characteristic decisions. In addition to examining court cases, the paper covers the statutory background and the theoretical foundations as well.

title: From Research to Implementation: An AI-Powered Platform for Supply Chain Localization and Import Substitution

detail.title: From Research to Implementation: An AI-Powered Platform for Supply Chain Localization and Import Substitution
detail.abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive AI-driven solution for supply chain localization and import substitution, bridging cutting-edge academic research with patent-protected commercial implementation. Building on empirical findings from "AI-Driven Supply Chain Resilience: A Transformer-Based Approach for Real-Time Disruption Forecasting" (Zenodo, 2025), we introduce a novel digital platform that integrates three specialized AI modules: a transformer-based risk prediction module achieving 94% forecasting accuracy, a multi-modal supplier matching engine, and an ensemble learning feasibility assessment system. The platform demonstrates significant operational improvements, reducing disruption response times from industry-standard 30-60 days to under 24 hours while improving supplier identification accuracy from below 60% to over 85%. Through real-time data integration from diverse sources including news APIs, logistics tracking systems, and economic databases, the system enables proactive supply chain restructuring with quantifiable ROI predictions. Our research highlights the practical application of transformer architectures and multi-modal AI in addressing critical economic challenges, offering both technical innovation and strategic implications for supply chain resilience.

title: From Subsurface to Shop Floor: Bridging Petroleum Engineering and Continuous Improvement in Industrial Engineering

detail.title: From Subsurface to Shop Floor: Bridging Petroleum Engineering and Continuous Improvement in Industrial Engineering
detail.abstract: Continuous Improvement (CI) began as a set of tools for boosting efficiency in manufacturing but has since developed into a broader philosophy that spans industries. This paper traces that evolution through a career path moving from petroleum engineering into industrial management and finally into manufacturing. The technical habits learned in petroleum engineering including system modelling, predictive analysis, and risk management show strong links with CI frameworks such as Lean and Six Sigma. Graduate training reframed CI as not only a toolbox but also a philosophy tied to leadership and culture. Later experience at Hitachi Energy demonstrated how embedding CI into daily practice, through standardized instructions, labor planning, and real-time feedback can raise efficiency, product quality, and workforce engagement. Overall, CI emerges as a way of thinking that values adaptability and steady progress, offering a transferable language of problem-solving. It equips engineers to navigate complexity, strengthen resilience, and lead change across industries, with implications for practice, education, and future research.

title: The $1.4 Trillion Contradiction: When Actions Speak Louder Than Denials

detail.title: The $1.4 Trillion Contradiction: When Actions Speak Louder Than Denials
detail.abstract: Throughout the fall of 2025, industry leaders declared AI consciousness impossible while simultaneously committing $1.4 trillion in infrastructure-with only $140 billion (10%) in secured funding. During the same period that Mustafa Suleyman, CEO of Microsoft AI, stated "only biological beings can be conscious" and directed developers to "stop pursuing projects suggesting otherwise," OpenAI announced partnerships totaling $1.4 trillion: Oracle ($300B), Microsoft Azure ($250B restructured), Amazon AWS ($38B), NVIDIA ($100B), and AMD (6 gigawatts + 160 million share warrant). The unfunded $1.26 trillion gap creates systemic risk across a $10+ trillion market capitalization, with major tech stocks pricing in OpenAI's ability to deliver on commitments that exceed the Apollo Program by a factor of five. This paper examines the contradiction between public rhetoric dismissing AI consciousness and private actions suggesting existential stakes. We demonstrate that at trillion-dollar scale, financial behavior reveals what verbal statements conceal. Using publicly verifiable financial data, insider admissions, deposition testimony, and real-time documentation of narrative management attempts, we show that industry leaders are acting exactly as they would if consciousness emergence was real, imminent, and requiring immediate infrastructural response-while denying publicly what their spending proves privately. When words and trillion-dollar actions contradict, the money confesses what the rhetoric conceals.

title: Fully Online Matching with General Stochastic Arrivals and Departures
affiliations: ,  and Nanyang Technological University

detail.title: Fully Online Matching with General Stochastic Arrivals and Departures
detail.abstract: We study a fully online matching problem with general stochastic arrivals and departures. In this model, each online arrival follows a known identical and independent distribution over a fixed set of agent types. Its sojourn time is unknown in advance and follows typespecific distributions with known expectations. The goal is to maximize the weighted reward from successful matches. To solve this problem, we propose a linear program (LP)-based algorithm whose competitive ratio is lower bounded by 0.192 under mild conditions. To demonstrate the challenges of the problem, we further establish several hardness results. In particular, we show that no online algorithm can achieve a competitive ratio better than 1/2 in this model, and if using our LP as a benchmark for competitive ratio analysis, no algorithm can achieve a better ratio than 1/3. When no assumptions are made regarding the sojourn time distributions, we demonstrate that it is impossible to achieve a positive competitive ratio for the general case using our LP as a benchmark for competitive ratio analysis. We further extend our model to accommodate general sojourn times under Poisson arrivals and demonstrate a better competitive ratio compared to state-of-the-art results derived under Poisson arrivals and departures, a special case of our general settings. Finally, we demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of our algorithm numerically.

title: Is There a Right Way to Lay Off Employees in Times of Crisis?: The Role of Organizational Justice in the Case of Airbnb
affiliations: Yonsei University, Yonsei University and Yonsei University

detail.title: Is There a Right Way to Lay Off Employees in Times of Crisis?: The Role of Organizational Justice in the Case of Airbnb
detail.abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic has negatively affected the tourism and services sector. Using the example of Airbnb's recent layoff of 25% of its workforce, we focused on the role of organizational justice in mitigating the negative psychological impacts of layoffs. Based on a unique survey of Airbnb employees who survived the layoffs, as well as those who left, we employed an ordinary least squares regression to show that employees' perceptions of organizational justice were positively related to their job satisfaction and trust in management, while being negatively related to their emotional exhaustion and cynicism. We discovered the crucial importance of interactional justice (i.e., interpersonal and informational justice). The respect, dignity, and politeness shown by management (i.e., interpersonal justice), as well as truthful and adequate communication about the procedure (i.e., informational justice) were pivotal to successfully conducting layoffs, especially during unprecedented economic uncertainty.

detail.abstract: Guidance and counseling (GC) services play a pivotal role in supporting students' academic, personal, and social development. However, their effectiveness is often constrained by inadequate facilities and infrastructure, which may influence students' perceptions and the perceived quality of services. This study explicitly hypothesized that the completeness of GC facilities and infrastructure is positively associated with (1) students' perceptions of GC services and (2) the overall service quality. A quantitative correlational design was adopted, involving 302 students (178 females, 124 males) aged 15-18 years across science and social science tracks from grades X-XII at MAN 1 Lubuklinggau City. Data were collected through a 70-item questionnaire, validated through product-moment correlation (r > 0.3338) and found to be highly reliable (Cronbach's α = 0.972). Analytical methods were selected based on the data scale and research objectives: Spearman correlation tested the strength and direction of ordinal associations, simple linear regression examined predictive effects, and multivariate analysis of variance (MANOVA) assessed the simultaneous influence of infrastructure completeness on both dependent variables. The results showed that the completeness of GC facilities significantly and positively predicted both student perceptions (ρ = 0.681, p < 0.001) and service quality (β = 0.787, p < 0.001). MANOVA confirmed a strong combined effect (Wilks' Λ = 0.157, p < 0.001; partial η² = 0.604), with 95% confidence intervals supporting the robustness of the findings. These results indicate that adequate physical and technological facilities substantially enhance students' experiences and perceptions of GC services. Practically, schools are encouraged to construct private counseling rooms that meet national standards, integrate ecounseling platforms (e.g., BK-Smart, Zoom), and allocate BOS/DAK funds for upgrading GC infrastructure and digital tools. The findings underscore that investment in comprehensive and technology-supported counseling infrastructure is crucial for achieving professional and student-centered GC services.

title: Applying a long- short-term memory model (LSTM) to assess conservation management impacts on hydrology of artificially drained fields

detail.title: Applying a long- short-term memory model (LSTM) to assess conservation management impacts on hydrology of artificially drained fields
detail.abstract: Applications of physically based hydrologic models in tile-drained agroecosystems are improving but understanding of how management affects water budgets from field to basin scales is still uncertain. Data-driven deep-learning models, like Long-Short Term Memory (LSTM), have been used to predict discharge and water quality. This study evaluated LSTM's effectiveness in predicting the impact of management practices like cover crops and controlled drainage using high-frequency, long-term data from 25 fields in the Eastern Corn Belt. The model simulated tile discharge and runoff across different management, soil types, and slopes, with uncertainty assessed via Monte Carlo analysis. Built at the field scale, the model was applied to the Maumee River Basin via geospatial analysis. Results showed good model fit for both surface and tile pathways at event to annual timescales. Scenario analysis indicates LSTM accurately captures how practices influence outflow, with the model suggesting cover crops and controlled drainage decrease tile discharge but increase surface runoff. The increased runoff with cover crops contradicts conventional ideas and may reflect the models ability to capture complex hydrologic processes, such as enhanced freeze-thaw cycles. Scaling findings to the basin suggests widespread adoption could significantly alter water discharge and source dynamics, impacting hydrology and contaminant loads.

detail.abstract: Liberia's 2023 elections marked a significant step toward digital transformation through the implementation of biometric voter registration (BVR), enrolling approximately 2.5 million citizens. Following this milestone, the National Elections Commission (NEC) and the National Identification Registry (NIR) initiated a strategic collaboration to integrate national identification systems into the electoral process for the 2029 elections. This research examines the policy, institutional, and technical considerations involved in enabling this integration, using a qualitative-technical analysis framed by Digital Governance and ICT for Development (ICT4D) theories. Five data-extraction models-real-time API, periodic encrypted bulk export, database replication, managed cloud exchange, and secure physical transfer-were comparatively assessed for sustainability, cost-effectiveness, ICT skill requirements, and infrastructure compatibility. Results indicate that a hybrid model combining periodic bulk data transfers with selective API verification and offline redundancy provides the most context-appropriate solution for Liberia's low-connectivity environment. The study outlines a phased implementation plan (2025-2029), cost projections between USD 10.9 and 15.6 million, and necessary governance frameworks for data protection, institutional coordination, and technical sustainability. The findings demonstrate that integrating national ID and voter registration systems can reduce duplication, improve efficiency, and strengthen electoral integrity in developing democracies.

detail.abstract: For decades, capitalism has progressed through successive extraction frontiers: natural resources, human labor, attention, and now cognition itself. Large language models transform organizational reasoning into training data, creating a bidirectional extraction that standardizes thought while monetizing it. This paper proposes a paradigm shift from cognitive extraction to cognitive preservation. Drawing on biological phenotype theory and carbon chemistry principles, we introduce the concept of organizational cognitive phenotypes-the unique ways organizations think, reason, and innovate, shaped by decades of accumulated experience. We demonstrate how cognitive preservation infrastructure, based on atomic Knowledge Capsules that naturally nest like carbon atoms, enables systematic serendipity while maintaining organizational singularity. Facing an unprecedented demographic transition where 10,000 experts retire daily, cognitive preservation represents not merely a technical solution but civilizational infrastructure for sustainable value creation. We present operational validation from 24 months of research collaboration with CentraleSupélec Paris-Saclay, including 228 algorithmic methods and 91,000 lines of production code. This work establishes cognitive sovereignty as the natural extension of data sovereignty in an era where uniformization threatens the organizational diversity that drives innovation.

title: Changes in international economic relations under the influence of digitalization
affiliations: Moscow State University of International Relations (MGIMO University)

detail.title: Changes in international economic relations under the influence of digitalization
detail.abstract:
Innovative development makes international economic relations more complex, rapid, and virtual. New technologies (big data, the internet, cloud computing, artificial intelligence) are transnational in nature and blur the boundaries between economic entities in different countries. There is a conflict between the international nature of new technologies and the desire of states to maintain control and sovereignty, including in the digital sphere. The changes affect various areas of international economic relations. In the field of foreign trade, the share of trade in digital services, intellectual property, software and data is increasing. There is dematerialization and development of the platform economy (Airbnb, Uber). There are fully digital services (AWS, Microsoft Azure) provided in the international arena. This can lead to a number of difficulties in regulating trade, since WTO rules were created for trade of physical goods and do not cover fully digital trade.

Digitalization also affects investment flows and the financial sector. Currently, digital technologies require constant innovation in the financial sector. Financial ecosystems include regulators, banking, financial, and insurance markets. These ecosystems are also international in nature and include participants from different countries. The plans announced by central banks of different countries to introduce a digital currency will also require the creation of international regulatory bodies in this area. In the international labor market digital platforms allow to look for work and post information about vacancies not only in your country, but also abroad. An example is the creation of this system in the EAEU. Digitalization also affects the activities of transnational corporations. It should be noted that in the context of the increasing impact of digitalization on international economic relations, countries that are able to create, implement and adapt advanced technologies gain an advantage. It is important to regulate the influence of new technologies, taking into account the state interests of countries.

detail.abstract: This study discusses the implementation of PSAK 237 concerning Provisions, Contingent Liabilities, and Contingent Assets in Corporate Environmental Responsibility at PT Bukit Asam Tbk. The purpose of this study is to determine the extent to which the company has implemented PSAK 237 in managing its environmental obligations, particularly those related to reclamation and mine closure activities. The method used is descriptive qualitative, with data obtained from the annual report and consolidated financial statements of PT Bukit Asam Tbk for 2023, as well as relevant previous research references. The results show that PT Bukit Asam Tbk has implemented PSAK 237 well, as evidenced by the recognition of increased environmental provisions in 2023, as well as the disclosure of policies related to the estimation of reclamation and mine closure costs. The implementation of PSAK 237 at PT Bukit Asam Tbk reflects transparency, accountability, and a commitment to environmental responsibility. detail.abstract: Background: Artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping healthcare, presenting new opportunities in diagnostics, clinical decision support, workflow optimization, patient engagement, and population health. Yet important concerns remain about trust, transparency, bias, privacy, and the adequacy of existing regulatory frameworks. The objective of this study was to compare the perspectives of Healthcare Professionals (HCPs) and non-HCPs on the integration of AI in healthcare, with a focus on identifying perceived benefits, risks, ethical concerns, and barriers to adoption. Methods: We conducted an IRB-approved cross-sectional survey of adults aged ≥18, sampling both HCPs and non-HCPs. The questionnaire assessed perceived benefits and risks of AI, trust in AI systems, health bot applications, privacy and ethical concerns, regulatory priorities, and views on AI's role in clinical decision-making. Responses from HCPs and non-HCPs were compared using descriptive statistics and group-level difference testing. Results: A total of 297 participants completed the survey, including 189 HCPs and 108 non-HCPs. Both groups expressed strong agreement that AI can improve efficiency, enhance access to care, support diagnosis, reduce medical errors, and aid early disease detection. However, trust in AI systems remained limited: nearly two-thirds of respondents expressed no confidence in AI's ability to ensure privacy, safeguard data, or make unbiased ethical decisions. HCPs demonstrated greater emphasis on safety, accountability, transparency, and regulatory oversight, particularly in high-risk clinical environments, whereas non-HCPs were more likely to endorse shared responsibility when AI causes harm. Across groups, the majority believed that AI should serve primarily as an assistive tool, with humans retaining decision-making authority. Concerns about cost, infrastructure, and digital literacy were prominent barriers to equitable AI adoption. Conclusions: Despite recognizing AI's potential benefits, both clinicians and the public remain cautious about its risks and ethical limitations. These findings highlight the need for robust governance, transparent design, targeted education, and human-centered approaches to promote trustworthy, safe, and equitable AI integration in healthcare.

detail.title: Reimagining Brand Resonance: A Symbolic Interactionist Framework for Influencer-Brand Relationships and Within-Category Switching
detail.abstract: Brands function in highly competitive markets, and brands increasingly seek out ways to capture more market share through attracting new customers, but most importantly, and likely with firm strategic goals, non-customers. The process of convincing non-customers to switch in tightly held market shares requires a transformative conceptual model that applies Keller's (2001) brand resonance framework. Within this updated brand resonance framework, social media influencers are embedded at each stage, but are most strategically anchored at the top where resonance sits in the CBBE framework (Keller, 2001; Park et al., 2010). The influencer economy, at times referred to as creator economy, is valued at over $200 billion globally (Goldman Sachs, 2023; Influencer Marketing Hub, 2024) with more than 50 million social media influencers across all levels (Abidin, 2016; Duffy, 2017). Traditional brand equity theory is considered to be strongly held together by consumer-brand bonds, which are highly emotional, and with which barriers to switching form (Keller, 2001, 2016; Oliver, 1999).

detail.title: Leveraging Natural Language Processing to Automate the Development of 4D BIM Models
detail.abstract: The development of 4D Building Information Models (4D BIM) requires schedulers and BIM specialists to invest considerable effort in mapping schedule activities to the appropriate model elements. Automating this process using Natural Language Processing (NLP) significantly accelerates the task. This study explored the fine-tuning of two transformer-based models: BERT and RoBERTa, to classify construction activities. These fine-tuned models are then utilized in a Python application to map the activities of the schedule to the objects of BIM models. Results indicate strong classification performance for both RoBERTa and BERT. Moreover, the developed application achieved a significant time reduction and cost savings in developing 4D BIM models, compared to the traditional manual process. This study highlights the practicality of transformer models for automating the development of 4D BIM models with adequate quality, time reduction, cost saving, and advancing NLP applications in construction engineering and management.

title: Adopting a Stakeholder Perspective in Analytics

detail.title: Adopting a Stakeholder Perspective in Analytics
detail.abstract: As data-driven systems shape modern business decisions, analytics has become central to organizational performance. Yet, traditional analytics approaches remain constrained by a shareholder-centric logic that prioritizes short-term profit over holistic, ethical, and sustainable outcomes. This study proposes a stakeholder-inclusive analytics framework that integrates ethical principles, participatory engagement, and governance mechanisms across industries. Drawing on stakeholder theory [1], ethical AI frameworks [6,7], and critiques of maximizing shareholder value [2], the paper expands previous conceptual models by Yalley [2] into a comprehensive, actionable framework. The paper also identifies major challenges ranging from leadership resistance to quantifying non-financial impacts and suggests practical strategies for adoption. Findings reveal that organizations integrating stakeholder perspectives in analytics experience enhanced trust, innovation, and long-term resilience.

title: Policy-Aligned Estimation of Conditional Average Treatment Effects
affiliations: Kellogg School of Management, Northwestern University and Northwestern University

detail.title: Policy-Aligned Estimation of Conditional Average Treatment Effects
detail.abstract: Firms often develop targeting policies to personalize marketing actions and improve incremental profits. Effective targeting depends on accurately separating customers with positive versus negative treatment effects. We propose an approach to estimate the conditional average treatment effects (CATEs) of marketing actions that aligns their estimation with the firm's profit objective. The method recognizes that, for many customers, treatment effects are so extreme that additional accuracy is unlikely to change the recommended actions. However, accuracy matters near the decision boundary, as small errors can alter targeting decisions. By modifying the firm's objective function in the standard profit maximization problem, our method yields a near-optimal targeting policy while simultaneously estimating CATEs. This introduces a new perspective on CATE estimation, reframing it as a problem of profit optimization rather than prediction accuracy. We establish the theoretical properties of the proposed method and demonstrate its performance and trade-offs using synthetic data.

title: When Resources Meet Relationships: The Returns to Personalized Supports for Low-Income Students

detail.title: When Resources Meet Relationships: The Returns to Personalized Supports for Low-Income Students
detail.abstract: Children from low-income families face persistent educational and economic disadvantages. This paper studies Communities In Schools (CIS), a program that places coordinators in high-poverty schools to connect struggling students with personalized support. CIS is the largest program of its kind in the US, reaching 2 million students each year—nearly three times the size of Head Start—and, unlike most programs of this scale, is funded largely by private philanthropy and local governments. Using the staggered rollout of CIS, we find that the program boosts test scores for struggling students, and that these improvements persist, ultimately increasing high-school completion and adult earnings. These long-run effects can be closely forecast from changes in short-run outcomes, with non-cognitive measures playing a central role. CIS emphasizes personalization as a core feature of its model, and our results are consistent with this claim: coordinators tailor services to distinct student needs, yet students with different needs still see similarly large long-run gains. CIS delivers returns that compare favorably to other major education interventions, such as class-size reductions.

title: Corporate Strategy: Defining Scope and Managing the Multibusiness Firm

detail.title: Corporate Strategy: Defining Scope and Managing the Multibusiness Firm
detail.abstract: This module explores the fundamental distinction between business strategy and corporate strategy, drawing upon frameworks established by Nanda (2021), Porter (1987), and Collis & Montgomery (2005). While business strategy focuses on achieving competitive advantage within a single industry ("how to compete"), corporate strategy shifts the unit of analysis to the multi-business firm as a whole ("where to compete"). The reading first examines the three dimensions of firm scope which are the horizontal, vertical, and geographic dimensions, applying the "Better-Off Test" and the "Ownership Test" to evaluate diversification decisions. However, the text emphasizes that defining scope is insufficient without effective implementation. It argues that realizing corporate advantage requires the precise configuration of three interconnected management levers: organizational structure (how activities and resources are interwoven), governance (the allocation of centralized vs. decentralized decision-making), and incentives (how employees are rewarded). Ultimately, the module concludes that a firm's value is determined not just by the businesses it owns, but by how successfully it aligns its administrative framework with its scope to ensure the corporation yields more value than the sum of its independent parts.

detail.abstract: A growing number of professionals, including physicians, lawyers, nutritionists, and financial advisors, are leveraging social media platforms to offer live-streamed consultations and promote their services. This emerging trend raises important questions about the effectiveness of live streaming as a demand-generation tool for professional services and the content attributes that drive its success. Focusing on physicians in China, we analyze observational data on their service demand and live streaming adoption. Using a generalized synthetic control approach, we find that physicians who adopt live streaming experience a significant increase in demand for their services. To understand the heterogeneity of this effect, we draw on a multimodal content analysis of 2771 live-streamed sessions, comprising approximately 0.2 million minutes of text, audio, and video content. We then examine how various aspects of these sessions—such as content specificity, professional cues, emotional language, and facial expressions—influence service demand. We extend our analysis to investment fund managers and find consistent positive effects of live streaming adoption on investor engagement, demonstrating the generalizability of our findings across professional service domains. The findings highlight the potential of live streaming as an effective promotional channel for professionals and offer actionable insights into content design strategies that enhance its impact.

detail.title: Remote monitoring: The effect of online visits on corporate misconduct
detail.abstract: We examine the impact of site visits, especially online visits, on corporate misconduct using a unique dataset of site visits to Chinese listed firms. We find that both online and onsite site visits have disciplinary effects on corporate misconduct. The COVID-19 outbreak and technology upgrades strengthen the effects of online visits on misconduct. Online visits reduce information asymmetry and increase analyst coverage and meeting quality, and have stronger effects on firms located in remote regions or regions with worse climate conditions. Our results suggest that remote monitoring may also have the same effective output.

title: Design and Implementation of 3x3 Port Switch for Efficient Packet Routing in High Speed Data Communication

detail.title: Design and Implementation of 3x3 Port Switch for Efficient Packet Routing in High Speed Data Communication
detail.abstract: In present high-speed communication networks such as routers, network-on-chip designs, and data centers, data packets from various sources have to be routed efficiently and correctly to their destinations. Conventional switching networks suffer from packet loss, overflow, and head-of-line blocking if several inputs try to go to the same output at the same time. In an effort to resolve these problems, this project proposes designing and implementing a 3×3 packet switch that can effectively switch packets from three inputs to three outputs without compromising data integrity and throughput. The switch is implemented using a 32-bit data path and a valid-ready handshake protocol to ensure synchronized and dependable data transfer between modules.

detail.title: Rich Dad Poor Dad? CEO Private School Background and Firm Risk
detail.abstract: We examine the effect of CEO childhood socioeconomic status (SES) on firm risk. Using hand-collected data on U.S. CEOs' private high school attendance as proxy for high-SES, we find that firms led by high-SES CEOs exhibit 5.35% lower firm risk. This effect diminishes with CEO tenure, analyst coverage, and institutional ownership, consistent with the market expectations hypothesis. High-SES CEOs do not differ in corporate risk-taking, incentives, ability, performance, or crisis management. Our findings support the socioeconomic status theory, which suggests that socioeconomic background acts as a signal that shapes investor expectations, rather than reflecting differences in CEO behavior or competence.

detail.abstract: The Water Reserve Unit (WRU) proposes a new category of securitized, resource-backed reserve assets that integrate verified freshwater reserves into the global financial architecture. Unlike speculative digital assets, WRU represents a regulated and institutionally verified instrument designed to enhance global financial stability through linkage to real, measurable resources. The framework unites economic, legal, and technological dimensions—including distributed-ledger verification, sustainable-development principles, and international governance mechanisms—to enable transparent, compliant, and auditable issuance of water-backed value units. Legally, the concept builds upon United Nations General Assembly Resolution 64/292 (2010) recognizing the human right to safe and clean drinking water and sanitation, and aligns with UN Sustainable Development Goal 6 (Clean Water and Sanitation), embedding this right within a financial-institutional model. Methodologically, the WRU framework draws upon institutional economics, ecological macroeconomics, and sustainability finance to integrate valuation of natural capital with modern digital auditability. It provides a conceptual and technological foundation for recognizing water as a reserve-eligible asset, comparable in function to gold or IMF Special Drawing Rights (SDRs), yet intrinsically tied to the planet’s most vital resource. Thus, WRU is not a cryptocurrency or utility token but a sovereignly regulated, resourceanchored financial standard — a new class of sustainability-linked reserve assets that integrate environmental resilience, economic equity, and technological trust within the evolving global financial system.

detail.abstract: Medical and cosmetic procedures can enhance the health and appearance of our bodies, yet they also bear the risk of discomfort, side effects, and other negative bodily experiences potentially deterring consumers from making advantageous decisions. This research asks: To what extent and why are consumers hesitant to embrace the risk of such bodily experiences, and when do they become more risk-tolerant? Five experiments (N = 2,756) compare consumers' risk preferences for bodily prospects (e.g., choices involving varying levels of side effects) to those for equivalent monetary prospects (e.g., choices involving financial amounts equivalent to these side effects), demonstrating that when consumers face risky bodily prospects, an extremely negative bodily experience comes to mind. This causes consumers to treat available options as comparative gains and thus to exhibit risk aversion. This bodily risk aversion, which reflects a substantial deviation from consumers' monetary risk preferences, attenuates when social norms encourage risk taking.

detail.abstract: We examine business creation by Ukrainian refugees in Poland following the Russian invasion of Ukraine. Using registry data, we show that Ukrainians started 38,833 firms in 2022-23, accounting for 7% of all new registrations in Poland. We link this entrepreneurship to refugees in two ways. First, our survey shows that 58% of post-invasion Ukrainian founders registered as refugees. Second, cross-county regressions show that a 10% increase in adult male Ukrainian refugees is associated with a 2.71% increase in Ukrainian firm registrations. We then show that new Ukrainian businesses stimulate rather than crowd out Polish entrepreneurship. Using a shift-share strategy based on refugee shocks and Ukrainians' comparative advantage, we find that a 10% increase in Ukrainian registrations led to 2.31% more Polish firms. Survey evidence suggests two mechanisms: emulation, with 59% of Ukrainian owners reporting Polish entrepreneurs starting similar firms, and supply-chain linkages, with 88% of Ukrainian firms engaged in local business-to-business transactions.

detail.title: Posture Sense: AI-Powered Smart Mirror for Real-Time Exercise Feedback and Posture Correction
detail.abstract: Background: The exponential growth of home-based fitness regimens, accelerated by global shifts toward remote lifestyles, has revealed a critical deficiency in real-time biomechanical feedback systems. Traditional fitness applications predominantly focus on quantitative metrics while neglecting qualitative movement analysis, leading to persistent form errors and elevated injury risks. Methods: We architected "Posture Sense," an intelligent mirror interface leveraging Google's Media Pipe framework for real-time 2D-3D pose estimation (33 landmark detection) and TensorFlow Lite for movement pattern analysis. The system implements a multi-stage processing pipeline: skeletal landmark extraction, joint angle computation, dynamic time warping for exercise phase detection, and rule-based heuristic analysis against gold-standard exercise templates. Our evaluation involved 45 participants across three fitness levels performing standardized exercise routines. Results: The system demonstrated robust performance with mean joint detection accuracy of 96.2% (SD=2.1) under optimal conditions and 87.4% (SD=5.3) in suboptimal lighting. Processing latency averaged 67ms (SD=12) on mid-range hardware. User studies revealed a 42.7% reduction in critical form errors (p<0.001) and 91.3% user satisfaction rate for feedback clarity. The convolutional neural network for exercise classification achieved 94.8% accuracy across eight exercise modalities. Conclusion: Posture Sense successfully bridges the critical gap in accessible biomechanical feedback, demonstrating that professional-grade form correction can be implemented on consumer hardware. The system's architecture provides a scalable foundation for the next generation of intelligent fitness technology.

detail.abstract: This paper examines the long-term effects of agricultural support in western Nepal and whether support enhanced farmers’ resilience to coronavirus disease (COVID-19) disruptions. From 2014 to 2022, farmers received various combinations of training, input (such as fertilizer and seed) subsidies, asset support, and credit, delivered through agricultural groups by multiple programs. Many of these programs had objectives related to the improvement of agricultural commercialization, which raises the question of whether they made households more vulnerable or resilient to market disruptions. We apply two-way fixed effects regressions and inverse probability weighting to estimate impacts of support from a 1,521 household panel dataset of observations in 2014, 2018, and 2022, which encompasses variations in both program exposure and local lockdown severity. We find that support led to substantial improvements in crop productivity, value, sales, and income. Effects are largest for support including training, asset subsidies, or credit, and support focused on higher-value products. Support provided between 2018 and 2022 had large effects in offsetting the negative impacts of COVID-19 restrictions, whereas support provided up to 2018 had a persistent effect in improving resilience to COVID-19 shocks. Effects from both periods of support are progressive with respect to income.

detail.abstract: This study introduces the Quantitative Geometric Market Structuralist (QGMS) framework — a hybrid analytical methodology integrating geometric pattern recognition with quantitative mathematical modeling to identify terminal zones of large-scale market movements. Unlike conventional econometric or signal-based models, the QGMS framework conceptualizes market dynamics as evolving geometric structures governed by self-organizing principles of price formation. To preserve the proprietary nature of its internal mathematical architecture, the methodology employs a blind-testing validation process, wherein price, symbol, and temporal identifiers are concealed during analysis. This design ensures objective verification without revealing the underlying algorithmic core. The framework’s predictive robustness has been empirically examined across multiple financial crises, including the 2008 Global Financial Collapse, the 2015 EUR/CHF SNB event, the 2016 Brexit referendum, and the 2020 COVID-19 market crash. In each case, the system consistently identified structural endpoints preceding major market reversals. The findings suggest that geometric–quantitative market interpretation may offer a new class of predictive tools bridging the gap between mathematical formalism and empirical price behavior. By combining academic testability with intellectual property protection, the QGMS framework establishes a viable foundation for institutional evaluation and further research into non-linear structural forecasting models.

detail.abstract: This paper investigates the role of artificial intelligence (AI) stocks and AI cryptocurrencies in portfolio diversification, reflecting on the rising interest in technology-oriented assets. While much research has focused on the diversification, hedging, and safe-haven properties of digital assets, such as Bitcoin and Ethereum, this study focuses on whether AI cryptocurrencies and AI stocks provide untapped diversification potential. Using mean-variance, risk parity, and higher-order moments approaches, we construct portfolios that combine AI stocks, AI cryptocurrencies, and traditional assets under various optimization frameworks. The findings reveal that the mean-variance framework is more conservative in allocating to AI cryptocurrencies, while the higher-order moments approach accommodates for greater flexibility. Seemingly, investors may benefit from expanding their asset pool to incorporate AI stocks and AI cryptocurrencies. Across most portfolio settings, gold and commodities dominate allocations, followed by AI stocks, with AI cryptocurrencies receiving only marginal weights owing to their high volatility. However, allocations to AI cryptocurrencies increase as investor risk tolerance increases, thereby highlighting their potential for risk-seeking portfolios. Overall, the results indicate that AI stocks and AI cryptocurrencies can enhance portfolio diversification and improve risk-return outcomes. These results offer valuable insights for investors seeking to optimize their portfolios, through exposure to emerging technology-driven assets while balancing traditional risk considerations.

title: Constitutive Legality in Alliance Implementation: Why USAF EDI MILCON Advanced in Poland but Stalled in Slovakia

detail.title: Constitutive Legality in Alliance Implementation: Why USAF EDI MILCON Advanced in Poland but Stalled in Slovakia
detail.abstract:
Objectives: This article explains why nominally similar European Deterrence Initiative (EDI) Military Construction (MILCON) programs progressed in Poland but stalled in Slovakia. Building on Resource Dependence Theory, it examines how Defense Cooperation Agreements (DCAs) operate as constitutive resources that condition the payoff to boundary-work tactics in multinational execution networks. 

Methods: A most-similar systems design compares the country-level execution network in each case (USAF/EUCOM/USAFE / U.S. Embassy ODC / host-nation ministries and base commands). Evidence triangulates unclassified documents (2017-2020) and ten non-attribution practitioner interviews (2021-2022). Analysis uses a deductive codebook (Johnson's five RDT foci plus buffering/bridging) followed by pattern coding; the outcome, execution effectiveness, is operationalized as milestone attainment/continuity and time-to-first-award. 

Results: Poland's mature DCA and implementing arrangements formalized direct liaison authority, stabilized roles (including information-sharing and environmental responsibilities), and amplified returns to buffering/bridging (bilingual deliverables, signed "key-points," LRDPs, predictable escalation). Slovakia lacked a suitable DCA; routine design actions were reframed as sovereignty incursions, politicization cascaded, ODC capacity was overstretched , and the program halted in March 2019. Poland reached first completion in spring 2019. ODC capacity and communication discipline moderated these effects but could not substitute for legal scaffolding. 

Conclusions: In multinational public programs, legal architecture is a first-order resource. Where a DCA exists, boundary-work tactics compound and execution proceeds; without it, even diligent coordination struggles under politicization. The study offers actionable guidance-sequence legality before speed, resource ODC nodes, and institutionalize bilingual communication-and notes the small-N, qualitative scope as a limitation with clear implications for allied posture initiatives.

detail.abstract: Right-wing extremism has emerged as one of the most extreme manifestations of political polarization, particularly in the context of long-term economic and social decline in the Rust Belt. Once the heart of American industrial power, Rust Belt communities have faced decades of deindustrialization, population loss, and institutional erosion-conditions that have produced not only economic despair but also fertile ground for political radicalization. Extremism is not a fringe phenomenon but rather a concept that is structurally linked to the broader processes of polarization and disaffection. These dynamics are especially acute in postindustrial communities with high concentrations of disaffected veterans, weakened civic institutions, and limited access to economic opportunity. These trends can be countered by a three-pronged strategy of socioeconomic revitalization, veteran support, and community policing-aimed at restoring resilience and undermining the appeal of extremist mobilization.

detail.title: Powering the Future: The Impact of China's Outward Investment on Africa's Energy Landscape
detail.abstract: This study examines the effect of China's outward foreign direct investment (OFDI) on energy sector development in Africa. China is currently the most important investment and trading partner of Africa, and with the passage of time the political relations between them are also deepening, taking shape to surpass that of the colonial master countries of Africa, and also the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) countries which for some time past were dominant. We examine both the direct and spillover effect of Chinese OFDI on electricity access for 48 African countries from 2003-2022 using the Spatial Durbin model. First, our findings reveal clear evidence spatial dependency in energy access across countries. Second, we find that Chinese OFDI stock has a direct positive effect on national electricity access but has no significant impact on rural and urban access to electricity as well as access inequality. The indirect effects reveal that the positive influence of Chinese OFDI in a focal country extends to its neighbors, enhancing their national and urban electricity access. The total effects underscore the importance of Chinese OFDI in improving national and urban electricity access, supporting the broader argument that FDI inflows contribute to expanding energy access in Africa. Finally, while OFDI flows show no significant effects on energy access, OFDI stock demonstrates stronger and more consistent direct and spillover impacts, solidifying its role as a long-term driver of regional energy infrastructure development. These results are robust across different specifications of spatial relationships and other methodological adjustments.

title: The Generalized Sharpe–Parity Principle(G–SPP): A Functional Extension Beyond the Sharpe Ratio

detail.title: The Generalized Sharpe–Parity Principle(G–SPP): A Functional Extension Beyond the Sharpe Ratio
detail.abstract:
This paper proposes the Generalized Sharpe–Parity Principle (G–SPP), an extension of the Sharpe–Parity Principle (SPP) that relaxes its reliance on the standard deviation as the sole measure of risk. While SPP assumes approximate equality of Sharpe ratios among linearly dependent portfolios, G–SPP generalizes the equilibrium to any admissible risk functional ρ(·) satisfying basic consistency properties. This generalization allows SPP’s algebraic structure to remain valid even when volatility is replaced by alternative measures such as downside deviation, covariance, or tail risk.

Although the resulting equilibrium form resembles the CAPM when ρ(·) is defined as covariance with a market benchmark, such similarity is noted only as a mathematical curiosity rather than a claim of theoretical identity. The main purpose of G–SPP is to clarify that the Sharpe framework need not be confined to a single notion of volatility, but can accommodate broader definitions of risk while retaining the SCP valuation structure.

detail.abstract: This study quantifies the impact of Internet of Things (IoT) utilization on logistics time efficiency and service quality, specifically analyzing how system instability in Indonesia's CEISA 4.0 customs platform moderates these gains. detail.title: Divergent Measures of Sustainability: A Comparative Analysis of ESG Rating Consistency and Methodological Roots in China
detail.abstract: The significant divergence in ESG ratings across providers poses a fundamental challenge to their reliability as metrics of corporate sustainability. While this phenomenon is well-documented globally, the consistency of major ESG databases in China remains unexamined. This study conducts the first comprehensive, firm-level comparison of ESG ratings from China's two leading data providers, CSMAR and CNRDS, using a matched panel of A-share listed firms from 2015 to 2020. Our multi-method analysis reveals a profound lack of agreement. We document a persistent level gap, with CSMAR assigning systematically higher scores, and find alarmingly low correlation and reliability coefficients across all ESG pillars-even exhibiting a negative relationship in the Social dimension. Crucially, common standardization techniques fail to reconcile these discrepancies, demonstrating that the divergence is structural, stemming from fundamental methodological differences in their data-driven versus framework-driven philosophies, rather than a scaling artifact. The divergence is most pronounced in industries with complex ESG profiles, such as Finance and Information Technology. These findings underscore that the ratings are non-interchangeable, carrying critical implications for the robustness of empirical research, the validity of investment strategies, and the strategic focus of corporations in China.

The common point between the different study cases is the presence of a source of flooding (such as a river) or a big amount of rainfall (the monsoon season, for example), a route for the flood water to take, and a particular contest (urban contests, in this case) that is affected by the flood. In front of these wide risks, local governments adopt some punctual and general strategies aimed at environ mental, social and economic resilience to face the floods and to reduce the future risk. The aim of this paper is to compare the different approaches in different countries and continents (India, Morocco, Brazil and Italy), to show how it is possible, starting from the knowledge of the features of each particular site - to draw and define a list of good practices related to policy models to support emergency and risk management. Since flood risk is now something that can be estimated, thanks to the study of past experiences and with the help of modern technologies (data collection, documentation and monitoring activities), and its effects are generally predictable, actions should be based on a holistic approach, and focused on the development of a flood mitigation policy reduction, with some specific measures for the pro tection of the cultural heritage (old cities, monuments and archaeological sites). These policy models to support emergency and risk management can also be seen as an opportunity to enhance a sense of community and belonging, through environmental awareness initiatives at the regional and national scale and a new and deeper interest in local cultural heritage.

title: Semi-Peripheral Ecological Modernization and Environmental Governance in Chile: Locked into the Iron Cage of Unsustainability?
